results.title: Sound
results.text:
Sound is built in: the desktop's sound plays in the Andronix app, and keeps playing when you leave the app. **Mute** is on the desktop's toolbar and in the **Linux is running** notification. There's no microphone yet.

In Termux, sound works differently: see [Sound in Termux](/termux/sound).

results.title: Sound in Termux
results.text:
Your distro sends its sound to **PulseAudio**, a sound server that runs in Termux. Each time you start the distro (`./start-debian.sh`, `andronix start` or `andronix desktop`), Andronix makes sure PulseAudio is running, and installs it in Termux the first time if it's missing. There's nothing to set up.

PulseAudio only accepts connections from the phone itself (127.0.0.1), not from your network.

With [VNC](/termux/vnc), the sound plays on the **phone**, even when you're viewing the desktop from another device. VNC doesn't carry sound.

results.title: Sound in Termux
results.text:
1. **Start the distro once from a Termux session** (not with a one-off command like `./start-debian.sh ls`). One-off commands never install packages, so PulseAudio only gets installed by an interactive start.
2. **Check PulseAudio is running.** In Termux, run:

```bash copy
   pulseaudio --check && echo running
```

   If it prints nothing, exit the distro and start it again.
3. **Check the volume** in the desktop's sound settings, and on the phone.
4. **Look at the log:** what Andronix did with PulseAudio is in `~/.andronix/logs/termux.log`. Include it when you [ask for help](/termux/install-problems#still-stuck).

The Classic Modded OS editions set up sound their own way. For them and for installs from before Andronix 2.0, see [Sound on an old install](/pre-2.0/old-install-guides#sound-on-an-old-install).

output.title: Sound in Termux
output.text:
This page is for Andronix with **Termux**, on phones that can't run Linux in the app (Android 7, or no 64-bit ARM processor), or if you use the command-line installer. For Linux in the app, see [Sound](/use/sound).

Sound works out of the box in Andronix 2.0. Anything that plays audio in your distro, like a browser or a music player, plays through the phone's speakers or headphones.

## How it works

Your distro sends its sound to **PulseAudio**, a sound server that runs in Termux. Each time you start the distro (`./start-debian.sh`, `andronix start` or `andronix desktop`), Andronix makes sure PulseAudio is running, and installs it in Termux the first time if it's missing. There's nothing to set up.

PulseAudio only accepts connections from the phone itself (127.0.0.1), not from your network.

With [VNC](/termux/vnc), the sound plays on the **phone**, even when you're viewing the desktop from another device. VNC doesn't carry sound.

## No sound?

1. **Start the distro once from a Termux session** (not with a one-off command like `./start-debian.sh ls`). One-off commands never install packages, so PulseAudio only gets installed by an interactive start.
2. **Check PulseAudio is running.** In Termux, run:

```bash copy
   pulseaudio --check && echo running
```

   If it prints nothing, exit the distro and start it again.
3. **Check the volume** in the desktop's sound settings, and on the phone.
4. **Look at the log:** what Andronix did with PulseAudio is in `~/.andronix/logs/termux.log`. Include it when you [ask for help](/termux/install-problems#still-stuck).

The Classic Modded OS editions set up sound their own way. For them and for installs from before Andronix 2.0, see [Sound on an old install](/pre-2.0/old-install-guides#sound-on-an-old-install).
